newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo NBY fails to sell new tranche of bonds.
newsitem.headline: Yugo NBY fails to sell new tranche of bonds.

text.p: Yugoslavia's central bank has failed to sell any short-term bonds from its new tranche auctioned earlier this week and traders on Tuesday blamed the low interest rate offered for the failure of the auction.

The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) offered for sale on Monday a new 20 million dinar ($3.5 million) tranche of 30-day bonds at an unchanged annual 43.28 percent interest rate, an NBY official, who asked not to be named, said.
"The result of the auction only shows very poor liquidity of the banking sector, which is not motivated to buy bonds at a three percent monthly interest," the source said.
Traders insisted the low rate could not attract anyone.
"I had several buy orders, but my clients did not want to accept such low interest," a broker said.

Another possible reason for the failure of the auction was that the market was readying for the announced sale of the Yugoslav government T-bills of maturity similar to that of NBY bonds, but carrying a higher 4.5 percent monthly interest. The sale opens on May 12.
Traders cautioned the failed auction signalled that the NBY temporarily lost its only open market operations instrument.

"But nobody seems to be too worried about that. (NBY) will probably wait until next Monday and Yugoslav T-bills sale and then decide on a new auction. Nobody really wants either paper to compete with each other," a trader said.
The central bank first launched its short-term bonds late in November 1995, introducing its first and only open market operations instrument aimed at regulating liquidity of the banking sector.
Bonds used to serve as the bench-mark for setting the NBY's key discount rate, but over the past several months the discount rate has become more dependant on inflation movements.
The highest rate ever on NBY short-term bonds, issued mainly at 30-day maturity, stood at an annual 147.48 percent and was set for the tranche of bonds auctioned January 13.
